character._note: ownerRef deliberately carries NO `$ref`, and that is a known, MEASURED exception to ADR-062 rule 7 — not an oversight. gate-54 reports it as a relation-shaped property missing its canonical $ref. TWO remediations have now been tried and BOTH were measured to break the character create dialog, on the same assertion, with the same 1-failed/170-passed shape. ARM 1 (ef7346c, PR #289): add `"$ref": "player"`. `character.ocName` already declares `$ref: "player"`, and with a second player-targeted relation on the same schema the dialog no longer renders a player selector at all — tests/e2e/spec-coverage/detail-forms-admin.spec.ts `character create dialog exposes a player (ocName) selector` failed with `expect(locator).toBeVisible()` on `input[placeholder*="player" i]`, on two independent runs, and passes on development. ARM 2 (PR #306, 2026-08-10): add `"$ref": "player"` TOGETHER WITH `"visible": false` + `"readOnly": true`, on the reasoning that nc-vue's `fieldsFromSchema()` drops non-visible/readOnly properties as its FIRST filter — before any $ref is read or any selector resolved — so a hidden property could not contribute a second selector. That reasoning is correct about `fieldsFromSchema()` and still WRONG about the dialog: the same assertion failed with `element(s) not found`, 1 failed / 170 passed, run 31428015957. So whatever resolves the player selector does NOT go through the visibility filter — the collision is at SCHEMA level, not form-field level, and hiding the property cannot reach it. DO NOT TRY A THIRD VARIANT OF THE SAME IDEA. The next real attempt is upstream: nc-vue/OpenRegister must key relation resolution by PROPERTY rather than by target schema slug, so two properties may point at `player` at once. Only then re-add the $ref, and only with that e2e green. See ConductionNL/.github#231.
